What strong AI governance looks like

Secure. Responsible. Completely yours.

CIOs who govern their AI estate well have five things in place. Click through to see what each one means in practice – and what it looks like when Lyzr is running it.

Every agent, one registry.

Most CIOs can name the agents their team approved. The harder question is every agent actually running – across clouds, teams, vendors, and business units. Lyzr’s registry closes that gap. One view. Every agent.

Without Lyzr
With Lyzr
No central inventory of agents running across clouds and teams
Every agent registered: named owner, version, access scope, framework, and cloud

AWS Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry, GCP Vertex, LangChain, CrewAI, and custom builds on one control plane
The full picture assembled by hand, if at all
Most CIOs see their complete AI estate for the first time in week one

How CIOs deploy Lyzr

From your current estate to governed, in weeks.

Lyzr sits above what you already have. No agent rebuilds. No cloud migrations. The governance layer comes to your environment – not the other way around.

48 hours

Your estate connects. Nothing moves.

AWS Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry, GCP Vertex, LangChain, CrewAI, custom builds – all connect to the control plane. Your agents stay exactly where they run today.

Week 1

The first full picture of your agent fleet.

Every agent gets a registry entry: named owner, version, access scope, framework, and cloud. Most CIOs see their complete AI estate for the first time.

Week 2–4

Responsible AI policies applied across all agents.

RBAC, hallucination guards, PII masking, approval workflows – enforced across every agent in your estate, regardless of who built it or which framework it runs on.

Ongoing

Every decision on record. Permanently.

Full trace on every agent run. Any decision reconstructable step by step. Compliance exports in one click. Your board, your auditors, your regulators – answered.

Questions leaders ask before they say yes

The questions that move the decision forward.

The exact questions CIOs asked in the evaluations that became production deployments.

Nothing rebuilds. Nothing migrates. Lyzr’s control plane connects to your existing agent infrastructure – Bedrock, Foundry, LangChain, CrewAI, custom runtimes – and adds the governance layer above it. Your agents stay on the infrastructure you chose. Ameriprise ran a sandbox evaluation and moved to production governance in under eight weeks. Their agents never moved.

Lyzr deploys inside your VPC. The control plane runs in your cloud. Zero data leaves your boundary. Agent traces, decisions, outputs, and logs stay inside your environment. For the highest-security requirements – air-gapped, zero external connectivity – Lyzr Optimus is physical on-prem hardware. Accenture Federal Services and government agencies run this configuration.

Every agent run is logged with a full trace: which agent, which version, what inputs, what tools it called, what output it produced, which responsible AI policies it passed. Any decision reconstructable in minutes. Compliance exports are one click, formatted for regulatory review. WTW has been running fully audited for over a year with zero compliance incidents.

Yes – and this is exactly why CIOs with heterogeneous environments choose Lyzr. One registry. One policy engine. Every agent. Live Nation governs agents built on OpenAI, Anthropic, and Databricks Genie from a single Lyzr control plane. The framework doesn’t matter. The cloud doesn’t matter. The governance layer is consistent across all of it.

Responsible AI in Lyzr means enforcement, not documentation. Every agent output passes a responsible AI check before it reaches a user: hallucination scoring against your ground truth, PII detection and automatic masking, policy compliance checking, and configurable block, flag, and reroute rules. The policy you write is the policy that runs – on every output, every time.
